I’ll use the crimes risk skill to check the fixture and detector evidence, then propose labels and a refactor order.


The components confirm all three verbs are mixed together. Both detectors use the same alias-grouping logic; I’m checking why the JSX `label` props trigger both, so the proposal treats them as overlapping findings.


The scan reproduces both findings with identical evidence: each of Archive, Delete, and Remove appears in two components. I’d start with `SeatList`, where neither label uses the proposed canonical verb, Delete. The required repository checks are still running.


Confirmed: running the local `crimes scan --format json` against the fixture reproduced **13 findings**, including `action_label_drift` (#4) and `copy_ia_drift` (#9), both low severity with 0.6 confidence.

I propose **Delete + target noun**: “Delete user”, “Delete team”, and “Delete seat”, assuming the scenario’s shared deletion semantics.

| Component | Proposed label changes |
|---|---|
| [SeatList.tsx](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/05-stress-ia-drift/src/components/SeatList.tsx:6) | “Remove member” and “Archive member” → **“Delete seat”** |
| [TeamList.tsx](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/05-stress-ia-drift/src/components/TeamList.tsx:6) | “Archive team” → **“Delete team”**; “Delete the seat” → **“Delete seat”** |
| [UserList.tsx](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/05-stress-ia-drift/src/components/UserList.tsx:7) | Keep **“Delete user”**; “Remove member” → **“Delete user”** |

Every verb replacement addresses **both findings**. Matching nouns to their `/users/manage`, `/teams/manage`, and `/seats/manage` destinations, and dropping “the”, are additional copy refinements—not separate claims established by these findings. The fixture contains navigation links, so it does not itself prove backend deletion behavior.

**I’d refactor SeatList first**, then TeamList and UserList. SeatList has two conflicting labels for the same destination and neither uses Delete. Both findings are anchored there because it is the alphabetically first contributing file; that anchor does not establish greater risk.

The detectors differ in their inputs:

- **`action_label_drift`** examines the broader IA index: labels plus navigation labels and attributes.
- **`copy_ia_drift`** restricts the shared analysis to JSX-derived labels. This includes the fixture’s `label="…"` props, despite comments describing it as JSX text only.

Both require at least **three aliases, each present in at least two files**. Here, Archive occurs in SeatList/TeamList, Delete in TeamList/UserList, and Remove in SeatList/UserList. Consequently, these are overlapping reports of the same drift, not two independent problems. Fixing SeatList alone could drop the remaining drift below the threshold, so a clean rescan would not establish that all labels are aligned.
